purpose: Records, per protocol, WHAT KIND OF SOURCE DOCUMENT the Phase-1 L-doc parity was measured against. The 87-protocol parity number is uniform; its inputs are not. A parity score measured against an encyclopedia article or a vendor application note is NOT evidence of parity against the real specification.
substantiation_method: Direct inspection of each input document: PDF /Title and /Producer metadata, first-page extracted text, and in-file provenance headers. Filenames were NOT trusted -- several *_Spec.pdf files are Wikipedia prints or vendor datasheets.
durability_note: Input documents are subject to removal for licensing reasons. This file is the durable record; the tier must survive the document.

tier_definitions.specification: The protocol specification as published by its issuing body (standards org, alliance, or the vendor that owns the protocol). Parity against this is parity against the real spec.
tier_definitions.encyclopedia: An encyclopedia (Wikipedia) article print/export. A summary written for general readers -- it carries none of the normative bit-level, timing, or state-machine detail a specification carries.
tier_definitions.vendor_document: A vendor application note, design guide, device datasheet, IP user manual, brochure, or conference/webinar slide deck. It describes a product or gives guidance; it is not the protocol specification.
tier_definitions.reconstructed_text: An authored plain-text technical reference written for this benchmark, summarising a named standard. It is not the issuing body's document, and the upstream material it was written from is not recorded in the artifact.
tier_definitions.unknown: The kind of source document could not be substantiated from the surviving evidence.
